steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key design movements: Art Nouveau (organic, decorative), Bauhaus (functional, geometric), Swiss/International (grid, clarity), Postmodernism (playful, deconstructed).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Understanding design history helps you make informed choices — every style has a context and communicates specific values.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Contemporary designers build on and react against historical movements — understanding the past enriches present practice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Critical analysis of graphic design considers: audience, purpose, context, techniques, visual language and effectiveness.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring graphic designers and movements. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with graphic designers and movements. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with graphic designers and movements. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to graphic designers and movements, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined  | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
